subtype: Approach: choosing the right moment and mood [Thinking]
passage: Emeka had the question ready at four o'clock: could he sleep over at Tobi's on Saturday? But Dad had just walked in with his shoulders low, phone pressed to his ear, talking about invoices. Not now, Emeka thought. Dad says yes when he is easy, not when he is tired. So Emeka did his reading, set the table and dried the plates. After dinner Dad leaned back with his tea and started the crossword. That was the moment. "Dad, have you got time for a small question?" Emeka asked. Dad looked up, smiling. "Go on." It was not yes yet, but it was "Tell me about it", and that was a start.

qa.q: What was Dad doing when Emeka asked his question?
qa.a: Dad was leaning back with his tea, starting the crossword.

qa.q: What was Emeka thinking about Dad's mood at four o'clock?
qa.a: He thought Dad was too tired and busy to say yes, because Dad says yes when he is easy and not when he is tired, so Emeka decided to wait.

qa.q: What else could Emeka prepare so the request goes well?
qa.a: He could have the details ready, such as where Tobi lives and when he will be home, since Dad is likely to ask about them.

qa.q: How might Dad have felt if Emeka had asked during the phone call?
qa.a: Probably irritated and distracted, since Dad was tired and busy, and he might have said no just to end the interruption.

grounding: A boy waits until his father is relaxed after dinner before asking about a sleepover.

subtype: Approach: choosing the right moment and mood [Thinking]
passage: Asif did his homework at the back of the waiting room of his father's small clinic, as he did every weekday. Yash's sleepover was on Saturday, and the question had been sitting in his throat all afternoon. At five the room was full: a crying baby, an old man coughing, the phone ringing. His father came out twice, rubbing his forehead, and took a call standing in the corridor. "Not now," Asif thought. "If I ask now, I'll get the tired answer." He waited. At home after dinner, his father leaned back with his tea and started talking about a cricket match. Asif slid in beside him. "Abbu, Yash has invited me to sleep over on Saturday. His parents will be home. Can I go?"

qa.q: Where did Asif do his homework?
qa.a: At the back of the waiting room of his father's clinic.

qa.q: What was Asif thinking when he decided 'Not now'?
qa.a: He was worried that a tired, busy father would say no, so he chose to wait for a calmer mood.

qa.q: What else could Asif add when he asks?
qa.a: The details Abbu might want, such as Yash's parents' number, so the decision is easy.

qa.q: How might Abbu feel being asked after dinner?
qa.a: Relaxed and more ready to listen than he was in the rush of the clinic.

grounding: A boy waits for his father to relax after dinner before asking about a sleepover, instead of asking at a tired, busy moment.

subtype: Approach: choosing the right moment and mood [Thinking]
passage: I'm Divyansh, and I was at Tanvir's house when he asked about the sleepover. His father came home at seven still on a work call, pacing and saying, "No, no, the delivery..." Tanvir started to get up, then sat down again. At dinner his father was quiet and kept checking his phone. Tanvir passed him the dal and said nothing. Later his father put the phone on the charger, stretched and laughed at something on the television. That's when Tanvir went and sat on the arm of his chair. "Papa, can I sleep over at Divyansh's on Friday? His mother said yes." His father said, "Let me call her, but probably yes." I don't know if Tanvir planned it, but it looked like he was waiting for something.

qa.q: What was Tanvir's father doing when he came home?
qa.a: Still on a work call, pacing.

qa.q: Why might Tanvir have sat down again when his father came in?
qa.a: He probably felt it was a bad moment and was nervous that a distracted father would say no.

qa.q: What else could Tanvir do if his father stays busy all evening?
qa.a: Ask the next morning at breakfast, or leave a short note, rather than catching him mid-call.

qa.q: How does Divyansh read Tanvir's timing?
qa.a: Divyansh isn't sure it was planned, but thinks Tanvir was waiting for something.

grounding: A friend watches a boy hold back his sleepover request until his father has finished work and relaxed.
